01
Before the first verse · Vol. 4, p. 634

Opening of the surah

Vol. 4, p. 634
Surah al-Muzzammil. Meccan [except verses 10, 11 and 20, which are Medinan]. It has 19 verses, and it is also said 20 [revealed after (Surah) al-Qalam]. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
سورة المزمل مكية [إلا الآيات 10 و 11 و 20 فمدنية] وآياتها 19 وقيل 20 [نزلت بعد القلم] بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 634
1. (1) . Mahmud said: "He is the one enfolded in his garments like al-muddaththir, and he was addressed with that which makes distasteful to him … etc." Ahmad said: As for his first statement, that addressing him with that is a disparagement of the state in which he said he was, and his citing of the mentioned verses as evidence — it is an error and a lack of manners. Whoever considers God's habit in addressing him with honor and respect will know the falsity of what al-Zamakhshari imagined. The scholars have said that he was never addressed by his name in the vocative, and that this is among his distinctions over the rest of the messengers, as honor and exaltation of him. So where is his being addressed with a disparaging form, by his name, and his citing as evidence for that verses that were said in blame of rough, barefoot herdsmen? I declare myself innocent before God of that, and I hold him ﷺ above it. I was reminded, by the saying "Sa'd brought them (camels) to water, while Sa'd was wrapped up," of something I came across in the words of Ibn Kharuf the grammarian, who rebuts al-Zamakhshari and faults his opinion in his work "al-Mufassal," and his excess in abridging the meanings of Sibawayh's words, so that Ibn Kharuf called it "al-Barnamaj" and recited against it: "Sa'd brought them to water while Sa'd was wrapped up; this is not how camels are brought to water, O Sa'd." As for what he narrated, that this was in 'A'isha's cloak ؓ it is far-fetched, for the Surah is Meccan, and the Prophet ﷺ consummated his marriage with 'A'isha ؓ in Medina. The sound view regarding the verse is what he mentioned last, because that was in the house of Khadija when Gabriel first met him; the sound hadiths have come to that effect. And God knows best. [.....]
2. . By Dhu al-Rumma. "Wa-ka'in": in the sense of "kam" (how many) of predication; its most frequent use is with "min," as in the saying "wa-ka'in min kadha." "Al-mutazammil" is the one enfolded in his garments when sleeping much. He says: Many a wasteland my she-camel has passed over and traversed, and many a sleeper and heedless one about its night — that is, the wasteland's or the she-camel's — lazy about the great matters in it. So "al-mutazammil" is a metonymy for that.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «هو المتلفف في ثيابه كالمدثر ونودي بما يهجن إليه
…. الخ» قال أحمد: أما قوله الأول أن نداءه بذلك تهجين للحالة التي ذكر أنه كان عليها واستشهاده بالأبيات المذكورة. فخطأ وسوء أدب. ومن اعتبر عادة خطاب الله تعالى له في الإكرام والاحترام: علم بطلان ما تخيله الزمخشري، فقد قال العلماء: أنه لم يخاطب باسمه نداء، وأن ذلك من خصائصه دون سائر الرسل إكراما له وتشريفا، فأين تداؤه بصيغة مهجنة من نسائه، باسمه، واستشهاده على ذلك بأبيات قيلت ذما في جفاة حفاة من الرعاء، فأنا أبرأ إلى الله من ذلك وأربأ به صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولقد ذكرت بقوله: أوردها سعد وسعد مشتمل ما وقعت عليه من كلام ابن خروف النحوي يرد على الزمخشري ويخطئ رأيه في تصنيفه المفصل، وإجحامه في الاختصار بمعاني كلام سيبويه، حتى سماه ابن خروف: البرنامج، وأنشد عليه: أوردها سعد وسعد مشتمل
…. ما هكذا تورد يا سعد الإبل وأما ما نقله أن ذلك كان في مرط عائشة رضى الله عنها فبعيد، فان السورة مكية، وبنى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على عائشة رضى الله عنها بالمدينة. والصحيح في الآية ما ذكره آخرا، لأن ذلك كان في بيت خديجة عند ما لقبه جبريل أول مرة، فبذلك وردت الأحاديث الصحيحة، والله أعلم. [.....]
2. . لذي الرمة. وكائن: بمعنى كم الخيرية، والأكثر استعمالها مع «من» كقول: وكائن من كذا. والمتزمل المتلفف في ثيابه عند كثرة النوم، يقول: كثيرا من المفاوز تخطته ناقتي وسارته، وكثيرا من نائم وغافل عن ليلها- أى: المفازة أو الناقة- متكاسل عما فيه من عظائم الأمور، فالمتزمل كناية عن ذلك.
02
Q 73:1–4 · Vol. 4, pp. 634–637

Verses 1 to 4

The verses as the commentary quotes them
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O you who wrap yourself in garments (1) Arise (to pray) the night, except for a little (2) Half of it, or subtract from it a little (3) Or add to it, and recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (4)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم يا أَيُّهَا الْمُزَّمِّلُ (1) قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً (2) نِصْفَهُ أَوِ انْقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلاً (3) أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلاً (4)
Vol. 4, p. 634
"Al-muzzammil" is "al-mutazammil," the one who has wrapped himself (tazammala) in his garments, i.e., enfolded himself in them, with the assimilation of the ta' into the zay; similarly "al-muddaththir" for "al-mutadaththir." It has been read "al-mutazammil" in the original form, and "al-muzammil" with a lightened zay and with fatha or kasra on the mim, as an active or passive participle from "zammalahu" — the one whom someone else wrapped or who wrapped himself. The Messenger of God ﷺ was sleeping at night wrapped in a woolen cloak, so he was roused and addressed with that which makes distasteful to him [1] the state he was in — wrapping himself in his cloak and preparing for heavy sleep, as one does who is unconcerned with any matter and not troubled by any affair. Do you not see the saying of Dhu al-Rumma: "How many a wasteland has my she-camel crossed, and how many a sleeper, heedless of its night, wrapped in his cloak" [2]
الْمُزَّمِّلُ المتزمّل، وهو الذي تزمّل في ثيابه: أى تلفف بها، بإدغام التاء في الزاى: ونحوه: المدثر في المتدثر. وقرئ: المتزمّل على الأصل والمزمل بتخفيف الزاى وفتح الميم وكسرها. على أنه اسم فاعل أو مفعول، من زمله، وهو الذي زمله غيره أو زمل نفسه وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نائما بالليل متزمّلا في قطيفة، فنبه ونودي بما يهجن إليه «1» الحالة التي كان عليها من التزمل في قطيفته واستعداده للاستثقال في النوم، كما يفعل من لا يهمه أمر ولا يعنيه شأن. ألا ترى إلى قول ذى الرمّة: وكائن تخطّت ناقتي من مفازة … ومن نائم عن ليلها متزمّل «2»
Vol. 4, p. 635
He means: the lazy, the laggard who does not rise to great matters and the sufficing of calamities, and does not burden himself with hardships and troubles; similar is: "You have for it a fierce-hearted, lean-bellied one, sleepless when the night of the foolish one sleeps" [1]. And among their proverbs: "Sa'd brought them to water while Sa'd was wrapped up — this is not how camels are brought to water, O Sa'd" [2].
يريد: الكسلان المتقاعس الذي لا ينهض في معاظم الأمور وكفايات الخطوب، ولا يحمل نفسه المشاق والمتاعب، ونحوه: فأنت به حوش الفؤاد سبطّنا … سهدا إذا ما نام ليل الهوجل «1» وفي أمثالهم: أوردها سعد وسعد مشتمل … ما هكذا تورد يا سعد الإبل «2»
Vol. 4, p. 636
So He blamed him for wrapping himself in his garment and made that the opposite of firmness and shrewdness, and commanded that he choose night-prayer over slumber, and girding-up over wrapping-up, and lightness for worship and striving in God. Of course the Messenger of God ﷺ girded himself for that with his companions in the fullest manner, and they turned to reviving their nights, abandoning for it sleep and ease, and strove in it until their feet swelled and their complexions turned yellow, and the mark appeared on their faces, and their matter reached a point where their Lord had mercy on them and lightened it for them. It is also said: he was wrapped in a cloak (mirt) of 'A'isha [1] praying; on this account it is not a disparagement but praise of him and approval of the state he was in, and a command to persist and be steadfast in it. From 'A'isha ؓ: she was asked what his wrapping was; she said: "It was a cloak fourteen cubits long, half of it on me while I slept and half of it on him while he prayed." She was asked: "What was it?" She said: "By God, it was not khazz, nor qazz, nor mar'izza [2], nor silk, nor wool; its warp was hair and its weft was camel-fur" [3]. It is also said: he went in to Khadija, terrified [4], the first time Gabriel came to him, with his shoulder-muscles trembling, and said: "Wrap me, wrap me!" thinking something had befallen him; and while he was in that state Gabriel called him: "O you who wrap yourself" [5]. From 'Ikrima: the meaning is "O you who have been charged with (zummila) a great matter," i.e., burdened with it. "Al-zaml" is the load; "izdamalahu": he bore it. It has also been read "qumi al-layl" with damma and fatha on the mim. 'Uthman ibn Jinni said: the purpose of this vowel is to get through it (the clash), escaping the meeting of two sukuns; so with whichever vowel it is vowelled, the purpose has been achieved. "Half of it": an apposition to "the night." And "except for a little": an exception from the half, as if He had said: "Arise less than half the night." And the pronouns in "from it" and "to it" refer to the half. The meaning: a choice between two things, between rising less than half the night definitively, and choosing one of two matters, namely reducing from the half or adding to it. And if you wish, you may make
فذمه بالاشتمال بكسائه، وجعل ذلك خلاف الجلد والكبس، وأمر بأن يختار على الهجود التهجد، وعلى التزمل التشمر، والتخفف للعبادة والمجاهدة في الله، لا جرم أنّ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قد تشمر لذلك مع أصحابه حق التشمر، وأقبلوا على إحياء لياليهم، ورفضوا له الرقاد والدعة، وتجاهدوا فيه حتى انتفخت أقدامهم واصفرت ألوانهم، وظهرت السيمى في وجوههم وترامى أمرهم إلى حد رحمهم له ربهم، فخفف عنهم. وقيل: كان متزملا في مرط لعائشة «1» يصلى، فهو على هذا ليس بتهجين، بل هو ثناء عليه وتحسين لحاله التي كان عليها، وأمر بأن يدوم على ذلك ويواظب عليه. وعن عائشة رضى الله عنها: أنها سئلت ما كان تزميله؟ قالت: كان مرطا طوله أربع عشرة ذراعا نصفه علىّ وأنا نائمة ونصفه عليه وهو يصلى، فسئلت: ما كان؟ قالت: والله ما كان خزا ولا قزا ولا مرعزى «2» ولا إبريسما ولا صوفا: كان سداه شعرا ولحمته وبرا «3» . وقيل: دخل على خديجة، وقد جئث فرقا «4» أول ما أتاه جبريل وبوادره ترعد، فقال: زملوني زملوني، وحسب أنه عرض له، فبينا هو على ذلك إذ ناداه جبريل: يا أيها المزمل «5» . وعن عكرمة: أنّ المعنى: يا أيها الذي زمل أمرا عظيما، أى: حمله. والزمل: الحمل. وازدمله: احتمله. وقرئ: قم الليل بضم الميم وفتحها. قال عثمان بن جنى: الغرض بهذه الحركة التبلغ بها هربا من التقاء الساكنين، فبأى الحركات تحرّك فقد وقع الغرض نِصْفَهُ بدل من الليل. وإلا قليلا: استثناء من النصف، كأنه قال: قم أقل من نصف الليل. والضمير في منه وعليه للنصف، والمعنى: التخيير بين أمرين، بين أن يقوم أقل من نصف الليل على البت، وبين أن يختار أحد الأمرين وهما النقصان من النصف والزيادة عليه. وإن شئت جعلت
Vol. 4, p. 637
"half of it" an apposition of "a little," in which case it would be a choice among three: between rising for the full half, rising for less than it, and rising for more than it; and the half was described as "little" only in relation to the whole. And if you wish, you may say: since the meaning of "Arise the night, except for a little — half of it," if you make "half" an apposition of "night," is "arise less than half the night," the pronouns in "from it" and "to it" return to the lesser of the half, as if it were said: "Arise less than half the night; or reduce from that lesser amount, or add to it a little," so the choice would be, beyond the half, between it and the third. It is also possible, when you make "half of it" an apposition of "a little" and explain it by it, to make the second "a little" mean half of the half, which is the quarter, as if it were said: "or subtract from it a little — half of it"; and you make the addition to this "little," I mean the quarter, half of the quarter, as if it were said: "or add to it a little — half of it." It is also possible to make the addition, because it is unrestricted, the completion of the third, so it would be a choice between the half, the third and the quarter.
نصفه بدلا من قليلا، وكان تخييرا بين ثلاث: بين قيام النصف بتمامه، وبين قيام الناقص منه وبين قيام الزائد عليه، وإنما وصف النصف بالقلة بالنسبة إلى الكل، وإن شئت قلت: لما كان معنى قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا نِصْفَهُ إذا أبدلت النصف من الليل، قم أقل من نصف الليل، رجع الضمير في منه وعليه إلى الأقل من النصف، فكأنه قيل: قم أقل من نصف الليل. أو: قم أنقص من ذلك الأقل أو أزيد منه قليلا، فيكون التخيير فيما وراء النصف بينه وبين الثلث. ويجوز إذا أبدلت نصفه من قليلا وفسرته به أن تجعل قليلا الثاني بمعنى نصف النصف: وهو الربع، كأنه قيل. أو انقص منه قليلا نصفه. وتجعل المزيد على هذا القليل، أعنى الربع، نصف الربع كأنه قيل: أو زد عليه قليلا نصفه. ويجوز أن تجعل الزيادة لكونها مطلقة تتمة الثلث، فيكون تخييرا بين النصف والثلث والربع.
Question
If you ask: was the night prayer obligatory or voluntary?
فإن قلت: أكان القيام فرضا أم نفلا؟
Answer
I say: from 'A'isha ؓ that God made it voluntary after it had been obligatory. It is also said: it was obligatory before the five prayers were prescribed, then it was abrogated by them except what they volunteered. From al-Hasan: the night-rising of a third of the night was an obligation, and they remained on that for a year. It is also said: it was obligatory, and the choice occurred only in the amount, and then it was abrogated after ten years. From al-Kalbi: a man would rise until morning, for fear of not remembering what lies between the half, the third and the two-thirds; and some said: it was voluntary, by the evidence of the choice in the amount, and by His words, Exalted is He: "And from the night, pray with it as an additional (voluntary) prayer for you." "Tartil al-Qur'an": reciting it slowly and deliberately, making the letters clear and giving the vowels their full measure, so that the recitation resembles the "thaghr murattal" — the well-spaced teeth likened to the flower of the chamomile — and not rushing it nor reeling it off [1], as 'Umar ؓ said: "The worst journey is the headlong rush, and the worst recitation is the gabble," until the recitation in its continuity resembles the crowded, close-set teeth [2]. 'A'isha ؓ was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of God ﷺ; she said: "Not like this reeling-off of yours; if a listener wished to count his letters, he could have counted them." And "tartilan" is an emphasis on the obligation of the command, and that it is something the reciter must have.
قلت: عن عائشة رضى الله عنها أنّ الله جعله تطوّعا بعد أن كان فريضة. وقيل: كان فرضا قبل أن تفرض الصلوات الخمس، ثم نسخ بهنّ إلا ما تطوّعوا به. وعن الحسن: كان قيام ثلث الليل فريضة، وكانوا على ذلك سنة. وقيل: كان واجبا، وإنما وقع التخيير في المقدار، ثم نسخ بعد عشر سنين. وعن الكلبي: كان يقوم الرجل حتى يصبح مخافة أن لا يحفظ ما بين النصف والثلث والثلثين، ومنهم من قال: كان نفلا بدليل التخيير في المقدار، ولقوله تعالى وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ نافِلَةً لَكَ. ترتيل القرآن: قراءته على ترسل وتؤدة بتبيين الحروف وإشباع الحركات، حتى يجيء المتلوّ منه شبيها بالثغر المرتل: وهو المفلج المشبه بنور الأقحوان، وألا يهذه هذا ولا يسرده سردا «1» ، كما قال عمر رضى الله عنه: شر السير الحقحقة. وشر القراءة الهذرمة، حتى يشبه المتلو في تتابعه الثغر الألص «2» . وسئلت عائشة رضى الله عنها عن قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم؟ فقالت: لا كسردكم هذا، لو أراد السامع أن يعد حروفه لعدها. وتَرْتِيلًا تأكيد في إيجاب الأمر به، وأنه ما لا بد منه للقارئ.
Editor’s notes on these 4 pages
Vol. 4, p. 634
1. (1) . Mahmud said: "He is the one enfolded in his garments like al-muddaththir, and he was addressed with that which makes distasteful to him … etc." Ahmad said: As for his first statement, that addressing him with that is a disparagement of the state in which he said he was, and his citing of the mentioned verses as evidence — it is an error and a lack of manners. Whoever considers God's habit in addressing him with honor and respect will know the falsity of what al-Zamakhshari imagined. The scholars have said that he was never addressed by his name in the vocative, and that this is among his distinctions over the rest of the messengers, as honor and exaltation of him. So where is his being addressed with a disparaging form, by his name, and his citing as evidence for that verses that were said in blame of rough, barefoot herdsmen? I declare myself innocent before God of that, and I hold him ﷺ above it. I was reminded, by the saying "Sa'd brought them (camels) to water, while Sa'd was wrapped up," of something I came across in the words of Ibn Kharuf the grammarian, who rebuts al-Zamakhshari and faults his opinion in his work "al-Mufassal," and his excess in abridging the meanings of Sibawayh's words, so that Ibn Kharuf called it "al-Barnamaj" and recited against it: "Sa'd brought them to water while Sa'd was wrapped up; this is not how camels are brought to water, O Sa'd." As for what he narrated, that this was in 'A'isha's cloak ؓ it is far-fetched, for the Surah is Meccan, and the Prophet ﷺ consummated his marriage with 'A'isha ؓ in Medina. The sound view regarding the verse is what he mentioned last, because that was in the house of Khadija when Gabriel first met him; the sound hadiths have come to that effect. And God knows best. [.....]
2. . By Dhu al-Rumma. "Wa-ka'in": in the sense of "kam" (how many) of predication; its most frequent use is with "min," as in the saying "wa-ka'in min kadha." "Al-mutazammil" is the one enfolded in his garments when sleeping much. He says: Many a wasteland my she-camel has passed over and traversed, and many a sleeper and heedless one about its night — that is, the wasteland's or the she-camel's — lazy about the great matters in it. So "al-mutazammil" is a metonymy for that.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «هو المتلفف في ثيابه كالمدثر ونودي بما يهجن إليه
…. الخ» قال أحمد: أما قوله الأول أن نداءه بذلك تهجين للحالة التي ذكر أنه كان عليها واستشهاده بالأبيات المذكورة. فخطأ وسوء أدب. ومن اعتبر عادة خطاب الله تعالى له في الإكرام والاحترام: علم بطلان ما تخيله الزمخشري، فقد قال العلماء: أنه لم يخاطب باسمه نداء، وأن ذلك من خصائصه دون سائر الرسل إكراما له وتشريفا، فأين تداؤه بصيغة مهجنة من نسائه، باسمه، واستشهاده على ذلك بأبيات قيلت ذما في جفاة حفاة من الرعاء، فأنا أبرأ إلى الله من ذلك وأربأ به صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولقد ذكرت بقوله: أوردها سعد وسعد مشتمل ما وقعت عليه من كلام ابن خروف النحوي يرد على الزمخشري ويخطئ رأيه في تصنيفه المفصل، وإجحامه في الاختصار بمعاني كلام سيبويه، حتى سماه ابن خروف: البرنامج، وأنشد عليه: أوردها سعد وسعد مشتمل
…. ما هكذا تورد يا سعد الإبل وأما ما نقله أن ذلك كان في مرط عائشة رضى الله عنها فبعيد، فان السورة مكية، وبنى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على عائشة رضى الله عنها بالمدينة. والصحيح في الآية ما ذكره آخرا، لأن ذلك كان في بيت خديجة عند ما لقبه جبريل أول مرة، فبذلك وردت الأحاديث الصحيحة، والله أعلم. [.....]
2. . لذي الرمة. وكائن: بمعنى كم الخيرية، والأكثر استعمالها مع «من» كقول: وكائن من كذا. والمتزمل المتلفف في ثيابه عند كثرة النوم، يقول: كثيرا من المفاوز تخطته ناقتي وسارته، وكثيرا من نائم وغافل عن ليلها- أى: المفازة أو الناقة- متكاسل عما فيه من عظائم الأمور، فالمتزمل كناية عن ذلك.
Vol. 4, p. 635
1. (1) . "I traveled at night in the darkness with a bold one, a hardy youth, not heavily burdened, of those whom women carried while girding (their waists) with the tight-woven belt, so he grew up not ill-fated; and free of every impurity except the menstrual remnant, and the corruption of a nursing woman and the sickness of a ghila. She conceived him on a frightened night, unwillingly, and her belt's knot had not been untied. So she brought him forth fierce-hearted, lean-bellied, sleepless when the night of the foolish one sleeps." By Abu Kabir al-Hudhali, describing Ta'abbata Sharra, whose name was Jabir ibn Thabit; al-Hudhali married his mother after Jabir and feared him, so she urged him (Ta'abbata Sharra) to kill him; he went out with him scheming for that but could not, and so he praised him for courage and sagacity. He says: I traveled at night in the darkness with a "mughshim," i.e., with a youth who plunges into a matter without concern, planning or fear of consequence, with boldness — "jald," i.e., firm and patient — "not heavily burdened," i.e., light in traveling, free of anything that causes weakness and slowness; and he explained it by his words "of those whom they carried," i.e., he is of those whom the women carried — that is, the kind of women — or he is one of the youths whom the women carried; and the pronoun of "bihi" is singular in regard to the wording of "man," and the verb "carry" is given the sense of "conceive," so he made it transitive with "bi"; otherwise it is transitive by itself. "Al-hubuk": plural of "hibak," like "khizam"; or plural of "habik" or "habika," which are the threads with which the belt is tightly woven. "Al-muhbal": one invoked against with "habal," i.e., bereavement and loss. "Al-ghubr" — with damma then shaddah — is the remnant of menstruation and the like; likewise "al-ghubr" with damma, and with fatha and sukun. "Al-ghabir": the remaining and the departing. It is possible that "ghubr" is the plural of "ghabir," and "ghabara yaghburu ghuburan," like "dakhala," means remained and departed, i.e., his mother did not conceive him in the time of a menstrual remnant. "Murdi'": one of the attributes specific to the feminine, and the usual practice is to strip it of the ta'; so what is here is contrary to the usual. "Al-ghila": a man's impregnating his wife while she is nursing her child, so that it falls ill; "al-mughil" is the one sickened by ghila. In the hadith of Muslim: "I was about to forbid ghila until I remembered that the Romans and Persians do it and it does not harm their children"; the analogy for "mughil" was that it be subject to the weak-letter changes like "muqim," "mubin," "mu'in," but it came in the original form irregularly out of necessity; and it is narrated "mu'dil," i.e., perplexing and baffling to physicians. "Za'adahu" — like "dha'arahu" — when he frightened him, so he is "maz'ud" and "madh'ur"; "al-maz'uda" is the frightened one, and the frightening of the night is a rational figurative expression, like "I drank the jug"; the fear in reality belongs to the woman. It is also transmitted in the accusative as a circumstantial clause, but then the mention of "night" would be lost, unless its description as "dark" is assumed. "Al-nitaq": what the waist is girded with. "Hush al-fu'ad" with damma: wild of heart, for its sharpness, its fire, and its aversion from people. The man "al-hush" and "al-hushi" is the one who keeps away from people, "mubattan," lean-bellied, slender. "Sahad" — with two dammas — is much sleeplessness, i.e., wakefulness; and attributing sleep to the night is a rational figure, for the sleeper is the "hawjal," the tall foolish man. And from the experience of the Arabs: when a woman conceives her child unwillingly and unprepared for intercourse, her child comes out noble. It is related of the mother of Ta'abbata Sharra that she said of him: "By God, he is the devil; I never saw him laugh, and he never set his mind to anything in boyhood but that he did it, and I conceived him on a dark night while my belt was tied" — and that indicates his nobility and courage.
2. . By Malik ibn Zayd Manat addressing his brother, who had consummated his marriage with his wife, and Sa'd did not manage the camels well, so he said: "Sa'd brought them to the water" while he was wrapped in his garments, not girded up. Mentioning the explicit noun in place of the pronoun contains a kind of rebuke. "This is not how they are brought," i.e., driven to water — he had been turning away from him, so he turned to him, and his calling him with the vocative of the distant implies that he is dull. The right of the "ha" of alert is to enter on the demonstrative noun, but it was put ahead of the kaf of comparison out of haste and concern for alerting. It is also transmitted, in place of the second hemistich: "O Sa'd, you do not water (them) like this, like camels." "Hadhak" is a demonstrative, and this verse became a proverb used for anyone who does not manage well the matter he has taken over.
1. (1) . ولقد سربت على الظلام بمغشم
…. جلد من الفتيان غير مثقل ممن حملن به وهن عواقد
…. حبك النطاق فشب غير مهبل ومبرأ من كل غير حيضة
…. وفساد مرضعة وداء مغيل حملت به في ليلة مزؤدة
…. كرها وعقد نطاقها لم يحلل فأتت به حوش الفؤاد مبطنا
…. سهدا إذا ما نام ليل الهوجل لأبى كبير الهذلي يصف مأبط شرا، واسمه: جابر بن ثابت، تزوج الهذلي بأمه بعد جابر فخاف منه، فأغرته على قتله فخرج به متحيلا لذلك فلم يقدر، فمدحه بالشجاعة والفطنة: يقول: سرت ليلا في الظلمة بمغشم، أى مع فتى يقدم على الأمر بلا مبالاة ولا تدبير ولا خوف عاقبة، مع جراءة، جلد، أى: صلب صبور غير مثقل، أى: خفيف في السير منزه عن كل ما يوجب الضعف والثباطؤ، وبينه بقوله: ممن حملن. أى: هو ممن حملن، أى جنس النسوة به، أو هو بعض الفتيان الذين حملت بهم النسوة، وأفرد ضمير «به» مراعاة للفظ «من» وضمن العمل معنى العلوق، فعداه بالباء، وإلا فهو يتعدى بنفسه. والحبك: جمع حباك كخزام. أو جمع حبيك أو حبيكة، وهو الخيوط التي يحبك بها النطاق. والمهبل: المدعو عليه بالهبل، أى، الثكل والفقد. والغبر- بالضم فالتشديد-: بقية الحيض وغيره، وكذلك الغبر- بالضم وبالفتح مع السكون. والغابر: الباقي والذاهب. ويجوز أن غبر: جمع غابر، وغبر يغبر غبورا- كدخل-: بقي وذهب، أى: لم تحمل به أمه في زمن بقية الحيض. ومرضع: من الصفات المختصة بالمؤنث، والغالب تجريدها من التاء، فما هنا على خلاف الغالب. والغيلة: إحبال الرجل امرأته وهي ترضع ولدها: فيمرض، فالمغيل: الممرض بالغيلة. وفي حديث مسلم: لقد هممت أن أنهى عن الغيلة حتى ذكرت أن الروم وفارس يصنعون ذلك فلا يضر أولادهم، وكان القياس في مغيل إعلاله كمقيم ومبين ومعين، لكن جاء على الأصل شذوذا للضرورة، وروى معضل، أى معى ومعجز للأطباء. وزأده- كذعره: إذا خوفه، فهو مزؤود ومذعور فالمزءودة: المخوفة، وتخويف الليلة مجاز عقلى: كشربت الكوز. والخوف في الحقيقة المرأة. ويروى بالنصب على الحال، لكن يضيع ذكر ليلة، إلا أن يقدر وصفها بمظلمة، والنطاق: ما يشد به الوسط. وحوش الفؤاد بالضم وحشى القلب لحدته وتوقده ونفوره عن الناس. والرجل الحوش والحوشى: الذي يجانب الناس مبطنا خميص البطن منضمره: سهدا- بضمتين-: كثير السهاد أى السهر: وإسناد النوم إلى الليل مجاز عقلى، وإنما النائم الهوجل: وهو الرجل الطويل الأحمق، ومن تجربة العرب: أن المرأة إذا حملت بولدها كارهة غير مستعدة للوطء: جاء ولدها نجيبا، حكى عن أم تأبط شرا أنها قالت فيه: والله إنه الشيطان، ما رأيته ضاحكا قط، ولا هم بشيء في صباء إلا فعله، ولقد حملت به في ليلة ظلماء، وإن نطاقى لمشدود، وذلك يدل على نجابته وشجاعته.
2. . لمالك بن زيد مناة يخاطب أخاه، وكان قد بنى على امرأته فلم يحسن سعد القيام بأمر الإبل، فقال: أوردها سعد إلى الماء والحال أنه مشتمل متلفف بثيابه لا متشمر. وذكر الظاهر مكان المضمر: فيه نوع من التوبيخ. ما هكذا تورد، أى: تساق إلى الماء، وكان معرضا عنه فالتفت إليه ونداؤه نداء البعيد: دلالة على أنه بليد. وحق هاء التنبيه: الدخول على اسم الاشارة، لكن قدمت على كاف التشبيه مبادرة واهتماما بالتنبيه. ويروى بدل الشطر الثاني: يا سعد ما تروى بهذا كالإبل. وهذاك اسم إشارة، وصار هذا البيت يضرب مثلا لكل من لم يحسن القيام بشأن ما تولاه.
Vol. 4, p. 636
1. (1) . His statement "and it is said he was wrapped in a cloak of 'A'isha": how, when the Surah is Meccan? ('A)
2. . His statement "nor mar'izza": "al-mar'izza" is the fine down beneath goat's hair — end of al-Sihah. ('A)
3. . I did not find it thus, and from his statement "it was not khazz" — al-Bayhaqi narrated it in "al-Da'awat" from her hadith on the night of mid-Sha'ban: "The Prophet ﷺ slipped out from my cloak." Then she said: "By God, my cloak was not of silk or qazz, nor linen, nor cotton, nor wool." We said: "Of what was it?" She said: "Its warp was of hair, and its weft of camel-fur."
4. . "His statement 'and he was terrified (ju'itha)'," i.e., frightened; he is "maj'uth," i.e., alarmed — so in al-Sihah. And in it: "al-bawadir" of a human and others is the flesh between the shoulder and the neck. ('A)
5. . I did not find it thus. Its origin is in the two Sahihs on the authority of 'A'isha ؓ.
1. (1) . قوله «وقيل كان متزملا في مرط لعائشة» كيف والسورة مكية. (ع)
2. . قوله «ولا مرعزى» المرعزى الزغب الذي تحت شعر العنز اه صحاح. (ع)
3. . لم أره هكذا ومن قوله «ما كان خزا» رواه البيهقي في الدعوات من حديثها في ليلة النصف من شعبان «انسل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من مرطى. ثم قالت: والله ما كان مرطى من حرير ولا قز. ولا كتان ولا كرسف ولا صوف. فقلنا: من أى شيء كان؟ قالت: إن كان سداه لمن شعر وإن كانت لحمته لمن وبر» .
4. . «قوله وقد جئث فرقا» أى أفزع، فهو مجؤوث: أى مذعور، كذا في الصحاح. وفيه البوادر من الإنسان وغيره: اللحمة التي بين المنكب والعنق. (ع)
5. . لم أره هكذا. وأصله في الصحيحين عن عائشة رضى الله عنها.
Vol. 4, p. 637
1. (1) . His statement "and that he not rush it (yahudhdhuhu) nor reel it off": "al-hadhdh" is haste; "al-sard" is continuity; "al-haqhaqa" is intensity of travel; "al-alass" is the close-set teeth. So al-Sihah states. And in it, "al-hadhrama" is speed of recitation. ('A)
2. . I did not find it from him through the narration of Mansur; rather, Abu 'Ubayd ibn Qutayba said in "al-Gharib": 'Umar said: "The worst recitation is al-hazrama." And al-Khatib narrated it in "al-Jami'" from the narration of Mansur ibn Ja'far, who said: I read to Abu Muhammad ibn Durustawayh; he said: We read to Ibn Qutayba with this. And Ibn al-Mubarak narrated in "al-Zuhd" from the narration of al-Hasan: "It used to be said: the worst journey is al-ja'ja'a." And Ibn 'Adi narrated it as a raised report from the narration of al-Hasan ibn Dinar from al-Hasan ibn Abi Hurayra; and al-Hasan ibn Dinar is weak.
1. (1) . قوله «وأن لا يهذّه هذّا ولا يسرده» الهذ: الاسراع. والسرد: التتابع. والحقحقة: شدة السير. والألص: متقارب الأسنان. أفاده الصحاح. وفيه «الهذرمة» سرعة القراءة. (ع)
2. . لم أره عنه من رواية منصور، وإنما قال أبو عبيد بن قتيبة في الغريب قال عمر «شر القراءة الهزرمة» وأخرجه الخطيب في الجامع من رواية منصور بن جعفر قال: قرأت على أبى محمد بن درستويه. قال: قرأنا على ابن قتيبة بهذا وروى ابن المبارك في الزهد من رواية الحسن قال «كان يقال: شر السير الجعجعة» ورواه ابن عدى مرفوعا من رواية الحسن بن دينار عن الحسن بن أبى هريرة. والحسن بن دينار ضعيف.
03
Q 73:5 · Vol. 4, pp. 637–638

Verse 5

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word (5)
إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلاً ثَقِيلاً (5)
Vol. 4, p. 637
This verse is a parenthetical statement, and by "the weighty word" is meant the Qur'an and what is in it of commands and prohibitions that are
هذه الآية اعتراض، ويعنى بالقول الثقيل: القرآن وما فيه من الأوامر والنواهي التي هي
Vol. 4, p. 638
onerous, heavy obligations upon those charged, especially upon the Messenger of God ﷺ for he bears them himself and burdens his community with them, so they are heavier on him and more oppressive. By this parenthetical statement He meant: that what he was charged with of night-rising is among the heavy, difficult obligations that the Qur'an has brought, because night is the time of slumber, rest and calm, so whoever keeps it alive must oppose his nature and strive against himself. From Ibn 'Abbas ؓ: when revelation came down upon him it was heavy on him [1] and his skin darkened [2]. From 'A'isha ؓ: "I saw revelation descend upon him on a bitterly cold day, and it would cease from him while his forehead streamed with sweat" [3]. From al-Hasan: heavy in the Scale. It is also said: heavy upon the hypocrites. It is also said: a speech with weight and preponderance, not trivial.
تكاليف شاقة ثقيلة على المكلفين، خاصة على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه متحملها بنفسه ومحملها أمته، فهي أثقل عليه وأبهظ له، وأراد بهذا الاعتراض: أن ما كلفه من قيام الليل من جملة التكاليف الثقيلة الصعبة التي ورد بها القرآن، لأنّ الليل وقت السبات والراحة والهدوء فلا بد لمن أحياه من مضادة لطبعه ومجاهدة لنفسه. وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنه: كان إذا نزل عليه الوحى ثقل عليه «1» وتربد له «2» جلده. وعن عائشة رضى الله عنها: رأيته ينزل عليه الوحى في اليوم الشديد البرد فيفصم عنه وإنّ جبينه ليرفض عرقا «3» . وعن الحسن: ثقيل في الميزان. وقيل: ثقيل على المنافقين. وقيل: كلام له وزن ورجحان ليس بالسفساف.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 637
1. (1) . His statement "and that he not rush it (yahudhdhuhu) nor reel it off": "al-hadhdh" is haste; "al-sard" is continuity; "al-haqhaqa" is intensity of travel; "al-alass" is the close-set teeth. So al-Sihah states. And in it, "al-hadhrama" is speed of recitation. ('A)
2. . I did not find it from him through the narration of Mansur; rather, Abu 'Ubayd ibn Qutayba said in "al-Gharib": 'Umar said: "The worst recitation is al-hazrama." And al-Khatib narrated it in "al-Jami'" from the narration of Mansur ibn Ja'far, who said: I read to Abu Muhammad ibn Durustawayh; he said: We read to Ibn Qutayba with this. And Ibn al-Mubarak narrated in "al-Zuhd" from the narration of al-Hasan: "It used to be said: the worst journey is al-ja'ja'a." And Ibn 'Adi narrated it as a raised report from the narration of al-Hasan ibn Dinar from al-Hasan ibn Abi Hurayra; and al-Hasan ibn Dinar is weak.
1. (1) . قوله «وأن لا يهذّه هذّا ولا يسرده» الهذ: الاسراع. والسرد: التتابع. والحقحقة: شدة السير. والألص: متقارب الأسنان. أفاده الصحاح. وفيه «الهذرمة» سرعة القراءة. (ع)
2. . لم أره عنه من رواية منصور، وإنما قال أبو عبيد بن قتيبة في الغريب قال عمر «شر القراءة الهزرمة» وأخرجه الخطيب في الجامع من رواية منصور بن جعفر قال: قرأت على أبى محمد بن درستويه. قال: قرأنا على ابن قتيبة بهذا وروى ابن المبارك في الزهد من رواية الحسن قال «كان يقال: شر السير الجعجعة» ورواه ابن عدى مرفوعا من رواية الحسن بن دينار عن الحسن بن أبى هريرة. والحسن بن دينار ضعيف.
Vol. 4, p. 638
1. (1) . Narrated by Ahmad from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas in the story of Ibn Umayya. He said: "When revelation came down upon the Prophet ﷺ they knew it by the darkening of his skin." And Abu Nu'aym in "al-Dala'il": "When revelation came upon him, his face and body darkened for it." And on this topic is the hadith of 'Ubada ibn al-Samit: "When revelation came upon the Messenger of God ﷺ he was distressed by it and his face darkened."
2. . His statement "and tarabbada" means he frowned. ('A)
3. . Agreed upon from the hadith of 'A'isha.
4. . Mahmud said: "It is said that al-nashi'a is the soul that stands at night, which arises from its bed … etc." Ahmad said: If you take "al-nashi'a" to mean the soul, then the attribution of concurrence to it is literal; and if you take it to mean the hours or the verbal noun, then it is by figurative extension [.....]
5. . "Nasha'na": we rose. "Al-khus" — plural of "khawsa'," the she-camel high at the top and heavy at the bottom. "Al-niy": fat. "Al-sura": night-travel. "Al-qamahid": plural of "qamhudwa," the top bone of the head. He says: we rose toward great she-camels whose fat the night-travel had melted and whose skull-bones it had stuck together — a metonymy for their being practiced in travel and accustomed to it.
1. (1) . أخرجه أحمد من حديث ابن عباس في قصة ابن أمية. قال «وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه الوحى عرفوا ذلك في تربد جلده» وأبو نعيم في الدلائل «كان إذا نزل عليه الوحى تربد له وجهه وجسده» وفي الباب حديث عبادة بن الصامت «كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه الوحى كرب لذلك وتربد وجهه.
2. . قوله «وتربد» أى تعبس. (ع)
3. . متفق عليه من حديث عائشة.
4. . قال محمود: «قيل الناشئة النفس القائمة بالليل التي تنشأ عن مضجعها
…. الخ» قال أحمد: فان حملت الناشئة على النفس فاضافة المواطأة إليها حقيقة، وإن حملتها على الساعات أو المصدر فهو من الاتساع المجازى [.....]
5. . نشأنا: نهضنا. والخوص- جمع خوصاء: الناقة المرتفعة الأعلى، الضخمة الأسفل. والى: الشحم. والسرى: سير الليل. والقماحد: جمع قمحدوة: وهي أعلى عظم الرأس. يقول: نهضنا إلى نوق عظيمة أذاب شحمها سير الليل، وألصق عظام رأسها بعضها ببعض، كناية عن تمرنها على السير واعتيادها له.
04
Q 73:6 · Vol. 4, pp. 638–639

Verse 6

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Indeed, the rising of the night is more effective for concurrence and more suitable for words (6)
إِنَّ ناشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئاً وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلاً (6)
Vol. 4, p. 638
"Nashi'at al-layl": the soul that arises (tansha'u) at night, which gets up from its bed to worship [4], i.e., rises and is lifted up, from "nasha'at al-sahaba" when the cloud rises; and "nasha'a min makanihi" and "nashaza" when he rose. He said: "We rose toward lean-flanked she-camels whose fat the night-travel had melted, and which had pressed their raised skull-bones close together" [5] — and the rising of the night, on the view that "al-nashi'a" is a verbal noun from "nasha'a" when he stood and rose, on the pattern "fa'ila," like "al-'aqiba." That is indicated by what is narrated from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr: I said to 'A'isha: "A man who rose at the beginning of the night — would you say of him that he rose 'nashi'a'?" She said: "No; 'al-nashi'a' is only the rising after sleep." So she interpreted "nashi'a" as getting up from the bed, or the worship that arises (originates) at night. It is also said: it is all the hours of the night, because they occur one after another. It is also said: the first hours of it. From 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ؓ both: he used to pray between the Maghrib and the 'Isha' and say: "Have you not heard the saying of God, Exalted is He, 'Indeed, the rising of the night' — this is the rising of the night." "It is more effective for concurrence": it is specific to it, unlike the rising of the day, in being greater in concurrence — the heart of the one who rises concurs with his tongue, if you mean the soul; or the heart of the riser concurs in it with
ناشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ النفس الناشئة بالليل، التي تنشأ من مضجعها إلى العبادة «4» ، أى: تنهض وترتفع، من نشأت السحابة: إذا ارتفعت. ونشأ من مكانه ونشز: إذا نهض، قال: نشأنا إلى خوص برى نيّها السّرى … وألصق منها مشرفات القماحد «5» وقيام الليل، على أنّ الناشئة مصدر من نشأ إذا قام ونهض على فاعلة: كالعاقبة. ويدل عليه ما روى عن عبيد بن عمير: قلت لعائشة: رجل قام من أوّل الليل، أتقولين له قام ناشئة؟ قالت لا، إنما الناشئة القيام بعد النوم. ففسرت الناشئة بالقيام عن المضجع أو العبادة التي تنشأ بالليل، أى: تحدث، وترتفع. وقيل: هي ساعات الليل كلها، لأنها تحدث واحدة بعد أخرى. وقيل: الساعات الأول منه. وعن على بن الحسين رضى الله عنهما أنه كان يصلى بين المغرب والعشاء ويقول: أما سمعتم قول الله تعالى إِنَّ ناشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هذه ناشئة الليل هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئاً هي خاصة دون ناشئة النهار، أشدّ مواطأة يواطئ قلبها لسانها: إن أردت النفس. أو يواطئ فيها قلب
Vol. 4, p. 639
the riser with his tongue, if you mean the rising, or the worship, or the hours; or more in agreement with what is desired of humility and sincerity. From al-Hasan: greater agreement between the secret and the open, because the sight of creatures is cut off. It has also been read "ashaddu wat'an" with fatha and with kasra. The meaning: greater firmness of foot and farther from slipping; or heavier and harsher upon the one praying than the day prayer, from his saying ﷺ: "O God, press down Your weight upon Mudar" [1]. "And more suitable for words": more correct in speech, and firmer in recitation because of the calm of voices. From Anas ؓ: that he read "wa-asvabu qilan" and it was said to him: "O Abu Hamza, it is only 'wa-aqwamu,'" and he said: "'Aqwam,' 'asvab' and 'ahya'' are one." And Abu Zayd al-Ansari narrated from Abu Sirar al-Ghanawi that he used to read "fa-hasu" with an unpointed ha', and it was said to him: "It is only 'fa-jasu' with jim," and he said: "'Jasu' and 'hasu' are one."
القائم لسانه: إن أردت القيام أو العبادة أو الساعات. أو أشدّ موافقة لما يراد من الخشوع والإخلاص. وعن الحسن: أشدّ موافقة بين السر والعلانية، لانقطاع رؤية الخلائق. وقرئ: أشدّ وطأ بالفتح والكسر. والمعنى: أشد ثبات قدم وأبعد من الزلل. أو أثقل وأغلظ على المصلى من صلاة النهار، من قوله عليه السلام «اللهم اشدد وطأتك على مضر» «1» وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا وأسد مقالا وأثبت قراءة لهدوّ الأصوات. وعن أنس رضى الله عنه أنه قرأ: وأصوب قيلا، فقيل له: يا أبا حمزة، إنما هي: وأقوم، فقال: إنّ أقوم وأصوب وأهيأ واحد. وروى أبو زيد الأنصارى عن أبى سرار الغنوي أنه كان يقرأ: فحاسوا، محاء غير معجمة، فقيل له: إنما هو فَجاسُوا بالجيم، فقال: وجاسوا وحاسوا واحد.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 638
1. (1) . Narrated by Ahmad from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas in the story of Ibn Umayya. He said: "When revelation came down upon the Prophet ﷺ they knew it by the darkening of his skin." And Abu Nu'aym in "al-Dala'il": "When revelation came upon him, his face and body darkened for it." And on this topic is the hadith of 'Ubada ibn al-Samit: "When revelation came upon the Messenger of God ﷺ he was distressed by it and his face darkened."
2. . His statement "and tarabbada" means he frowned. ('A)
3. . Agreed upon from the hadith of 'A'isha.
4. . Mahmud said: "It is said that al-nashi'a is the soul that stands at night, which arises from its bed … etc." Ahmad said: If you take "al-nashi'a" to mean the soul, then the attribution of concurrence to it is literal; and if you take it to mean the hours or the verbal noun, then it is by figurative extension [.....]
5. . "Nasha'na": we rose. "Al-khus" — plural of "khawsa'," the she-camel high at the top and heavy at the bottom. "Al-niy": fat. "Al-sura": night-travel. "Al-qamahid": plural of "qamhudwa," the top bone of the head. He says: we rose toward great she-camels whose fat the night-travel had melted and whose skull-bones it had stuck together — a metonymy for their being practiced in travel and accustomed to it.
1. (1) . أخرجه أحمد من حديث ابن عباس في قصة ابن أمية. قال «وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه الوحى عرفوا ذلك في تربد جلده» وأبو نعيم في الدلائل «كان إذا نزل عليه الوحى تربد له وجهه وجسده» وفي الباب حديث عبادة بن الصامت «كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه الوحى كرب لذلك وتربد وجهه.
2. . قوله «وتربد» أى تعبس. (ع)
3. . متفق عليه من حديث عائشة.
4. . قال محمود: «قيل الناشئة النفس القائمة بالليل التي تنشأ عن مضجعها
…. الخ» قال أحمد: فان حملت الناشئة على النفس فاضافة المواطأة إليها حقيقة، وإن حملتها على الساعات أو المصدر فهو من الاتساع المجازى [.....]
5. . نشأنا: نهضنا. والخوص- جمع خوصاء: الناقة المرتفعة الأعلى، الضخمة الأسفل. والى: الشحم. والسرى: سير الليل. والقماحد: جمع قمحدوة: وهي أعلى عظم الرأس. يقول: نهضنا إلى نوق عظيمة أذاب شحمها سير الليل، وألصق عظام رأسها بعضها ببعض، كناية عن تمرنها على السير واعتيادها له.
Vol. 4, p. 639
1. (1) . Agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, and it has preceded in (the chapter on) the Prophets.
1. (1) . متفق عليه من حديث أبى هريرة، وقد تقدم في الأنبياء.
05
Q 73:7 · Vol. 4, p. 639

Verse 7

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Indeed, for you by day is prolonged occupation (7)
إِنَّ لَكَ فِي النَّهارِ سَبْحاً طَوِيلاً (7)
Vol. 4, p. 639
"Sabhan": moving about and turning in your tasks and preoccupations, so that you are free only at night; therefore hold fast to communing with God, which requires freedom of mind and absence of preoccupations. As for the reading with kha' ("sabkhan"), it is a metaphor from "sabakha al-sufa," which is to fluff wool and spread its parts, for the scattering of concern and dispersal of the heart by preoccupations. He charged him with night-rising, then mentioned the wisdom in what He charged him with: that the night is more helpful for concurrence and stronger for recitation, because of the calm of the man and the hush of voices; that it is more collecting of the heart and more gathering of the scattering of concern by day, since the day is the time of dispersal of worries, division of thoughts, and turning about in the needs of livelihood and the Hereafter. It is also said: "free time and ease for your sleep and your dealing with your needs." It is also said: if something of the night escapes you, you have free time in the day in which you can make it up.
سَبْحاً تصرفا وتقلبا في مهماتك وشواغلك، ولا تفرغ إلا بالليل، فعليك بمناجاة الله التي تقتضي فراغ البال وانتفاء الشواغل. وأما القراءة بالخاء. فاستعارة من سبخ الصوف: وهو نفشه ونشر أجزائه، لانتشار الهم وتفرّق القلب بالشواغل: كلفه قيام الليل، ثم ذكر الحكمة فيما كلفه منه: وهو أن الليل أعون على المواطأة وأشد للقراءة، لهدوّ الرجل وخفوت الصوت: وأنه أجمع للقلب وأضم لنشر الهم من النهار، لأنه وقت تفرق الهموم وتوزع الخواطر والتقلب في حوائج المعاش والمعاد. وقيل: فراغا وسعة لنومك وتصرفك في حوائجك. وقيل: إن فاتك من الليل شيء فلك في النهار فراغ تقدر على تداركه فيه.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 639
1. (1) . Agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, and it has preceded in (the chapter on) the Prophets.
1. (1) . متفق عليه من حديث أبى هريرة، وقد تقدم في الأنبياء.

Q 73:8–10 · Vol. 4, pp. 639–640

Verses 8 to 10

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion (8) Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of affairs (9) And be patient over what they say and avoid them with gracious avoidance (10)
وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلاً (8) رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لا إِلهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلاً (9) وَاصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ وَاهْجُرْهُمْ هَجْراً جَمِيلاً (10)
Vol. 4, p. 639
"And remember the name of your Lord": and persist in remembering Him in your night and day, and be keen on it. God's remembrance includes everything of good remembrance: glorification, declaring "there is no god but God," magnification, exaltation, affirmation of oneness, prayer, recitation of the Qur'an, study of knowledge, and the like, with which the Messenger of God ﷺ filled the hours of his night and day. "And devote yourself to Him": and cut yourself off to Him.
وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ ودم على ذكره في ليلك ونهارك، واحرص عليه. وذكر الله يتناول كل ما كان من ذكر طيب: تسبيح، وتهليل، وتكبير، وتمجيد، وتوحيد، وصلاة، وتلاوة قرآن، ودراسة علم، وغير ذلك مما كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يستغرق به ساعة ليله ونهاره وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ وانقطع إليه.
Question
If you ask: how was it said "tabtilan" in place of "tabattulan"?
فإن قلت: كيف قيل تَبْتِيلًا مكان تبتلا؟
Answer
I say: because the meaning of "tabattala" is "battala nafsahu," so it was brought according to its meaning in keeping with the right of the verse-endings. "Lord of the East and the West": it has been read in the nominative as praise, and in the genitive as an apposition to "your Lord." From Ibn 'Abbas: as an oath, with the oath-particle implied
قلت: لأن معنى تبتل بتل نفسه، فجيء به على معناه مراعاة لحق الفواصل رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ قرئ مرفوعا على المدح، ومجرورا على البدل من ربك. وعن ابن عباس: على القسم بإضمار حرف
Vol. 4, p. 640
as in your saying "God, I shall surely do," and its response is "there is no deity except Him," as you say "By God, no one is in the house except Zayd." Ibn 'Abbas read: "Lord of the easts and the wests." "So take Him as Disposer of affairs": a consequence of the declaration "there is no god but God," because He alone [1] is the one to whom, by His uniqueness in lordship, affairs must be entrusted. It is also said that "wakilan" means "guarantor" of what He promised you of victory and ascendancy. The "gracious avoidance": that he keep away from them with his heart and desire, and differ from them with good manners, courtesy, tolerance and no retaliation. From Abu al-Darda' ؓ: "We grin in the faces of some people and smile at them, while our hearts detest them" [2]. It is also said: it is abrogated by the verse of the sword.
القسم، كقولك: الله لأفعلنّ، وجوابه لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ كما تقول: والله لا أحد في الدار إلا زيد. وقرأ ابن عباس: رب المشارق والمغارب فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا مسبب على التهليلة، لأنه هو وحده هو الذي «1» يجب لتوحده بالربوبية أن توكل إليه الأمور. وقيل وَكِيلًا: كفيلا بما وعدك من النصر والإظهار. الهجر الجميل: أن يجانبهم بقلبه وهواه، ويخالفهم مع حسن المخالقة والمداراة والإغضاء وترك المكافأة. وعن أبى الدرداء رضى الله عنه: إنا لنكشر في وجوه قوم ونضحك إليهم، وإن قلوبنا لتقليهم «2» . وقيل: هو منسوخ بآية السيف.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 639
1. (1) . Agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, and it has preceded in (the chapter on) the Prophets.
1. (1) . متفق عليه من حديث أبى هريرة، وقد تقدم في الأنبياء.
Vol. 4, p. 640
1. (1) . His statement "huwa alladhi": perhaps it should be "alladhi" without "huwa." ('A)
2. . Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih as a suspended report in (the book of) manners: "It is mentioned from Abu al-Darda'." And al-Bayhaqi connected it in "al-Shu'ab" in the sixth and fiftieth (chapter), by the route of Abu al-Ahwas, meaning the son of Ahwas ibn Hakim, from Abu al-Zahra', who said: Abu al-Darda' said. And Abu Nu'aym narrated it in "al-Hilya" in the biography of Abu al-Darda' by the route of Sufyan, from Khalaf ibn Hawshab, who said: Abu al-Darda' said, like al-Bayhaqi's narration.
3. . His statement "you need not get (al-zafar)": perhaps "in al-zafar." ('A)
4. . Narrated by Ahmad in "al-Zuhd" and al-Tabari by the route of Waki' from Hamza al-Zayyat from Humran ibn A'yan: "That the Prophet ﷺ (recited) this." And Ibn 'Adi narrated it from the narration of Abu Yusuf, from Hamza, from Hamdan, from Abu Harb ibn Abi al-Aswad. And others said that Yusuf narrates it from Hamza, from Hasab, from Humran.
1. (1) . قوله «هو الذي» لعله «الذي» بدون: هو. (ع)
2. . أخرجه البخاري في صحيحه تعليقا في الأدب: ويذكر عن أبى الدرداء. ووصله البيهقي في الشعب في السادس والخميسين من طريق أبى الأحوص يعنى ولد أحوص بن حكم عن أبى الزهراء قال قال أبو الدرداء. ورواه أبو نعيم في الحلية في ترجمة أبى الدرداء من طريق سفيان عن خلف بن حوشب قال قال أبو الدرداء مثل رواية البيهقي.
3. . قوله «لا تحتاج إلى الظفر» لعله: في الظفر. (ع)
4. . أخرجه أحمد في الزهد والطبري من طريق وكيع عن حمزة الزيات عن حمران بن أعين «أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بهذا» ورواه ابن عدى من رواية أبى يوسف عن حمزة عن حمدان عن أبى حرب بن أبى الأسود. وقال غيره: أن يوسف يرويه عن حمزة عن حسب عن حمران.
07
Q 73:11–14 · Vol. 4, pp. 640–641

Verses 11 to 14

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And leave Me with the deniers, those of ease and plenty, and give them respite for a little (11) Indeed, with Us are shackles and a Blaze (12) And food that chokes and a painful punishment (13) On the Day the earth and mountains shake, and the mountains become a heap of sliding sand (14)
وَذَرْنِي وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ وَمَهِّلْهُمْ قَلِيلاً (11) إِنَّ لَدَيْنا أَنْكالاً وَجَحِيماً (12) وَطَعاماً ذا غُصَّةٍ وَعَذاباً أَلِيماً (13) يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبالُ وَكانَتِ الْجِبالُ كَثِيباً مَهِيلاً (14)
Vol. 4, p. 640
When a man knows of his companion that he is anxious about a grave matter he wants to be spared, or about an enemy against whom he wishes to take revenge for him, and he is capable of that and able to do it, he says: "Leave me and him" — that is: you need not [3] get what you want and desire, except that you leave me alone with him by entrusting his matter to me and asking me to suffice you against him; for in me is what will free your mind and clear your worry. And there is no prevention, such that he would be asked to leave him with him, except the leaving aside of seeking sufficiency and delegating; as if, when he does not entrust his matter to him, he has as it were prevented him from it, and when he entrusts it to him he has removed the prevention and left him with him. And in it is proof of reliance that He is able to fulfil the utmost around which the addressee's wish revolves, and more than that. "Na'ma" — with fatha — is "ease of life"; with kasra, "bestowal of favor"; with damma, "delight." It is said "na'am" and "ni'mat 'ayn." They are the chiefs of Quraysh, who were people of ease and luxury. "Indeed, with Us" is what opposes their ease: of "ankal," which are heavy fetters — from al-Sha'bi: when they rise, they pull them down; the singular is "nikl" and "nakl." And of "Jahim," which is the fire of intense heat and blaze. And of food that chokes, which is what sticks in throats and cannot be swallowed — meaning the "dari'" and the zaqqum tree. And of painful punishment from among all kinds of punishment. So you see no one to whom their matter is entrusted, trusted with the matter between him and them, who takes vengeance on them with the like of that vengeance. It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ recited this verse and fainted [4]. And from
إذا عرف الرجل من صاحبه أنه مستهم بخطب يريد أن يكفاه، أو بعدوّ يشتهى أن ينتقم له منه وهو مضطلع بذلك مقتدر عليه قال: ذرني وإياه، أى: لا تحتاج إلى الظفر «3» بمرادك ومشتهاك، إلا أن تخلى بيني وبينه بأن تكل أمره إلىّ وتستكفينيه، فإنّ فىّ ما يفرغ بالك ويجلى همك، وليس ثم منع حتى يطلب إليه أن يذره وإياه إلا ترك الاستكفاء والتفويض، كأنه إذا لم يكل أمره إليه، فكأنه منعه منه، فإذا وكله إليه فقد أزال المنع وتركه وإياه، وفيه دليل على الوثوق بأنه يتمكن من الوفاء بأقصى ما تدور حوله أمنية المخاطب وبما يزيد عليه. النعمة- بالفتح- التنعم، وبالكسر: الإنعام، وبالضم: المسرة، يقال: نعم، ونعمة عين، وهم صناديد قريش، وكانوا أهل تنعم وترفه إِنَّ لَدَيْنا ما يضاد تنعمهم من أنكال: وهي القيود الثقال: عن الشعبي، إذا ارتفعوا استقلت بهم. الواحد: نكل ونكل. ومن جحيم: وهي النار الشديدة الحر والاتقاد. ومن طعام ذى غصة وهو الذي ينشب في الحلوق فلا يساغ يعنى الضريع وشجر الزقوم. ومن عذاب أليم من سائر العذاب فلا ترى موكولا إليه أمرهم موذورا بينه وبينهم ينتقم منهم بمثل ذلك الانتقام. وروى أنّ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ هذه الآية فصعق «4» . وعن
Vol. 4, p. 641
al-Hasan: that he reached evening fasting, and food was brought; this verse occurred to him, and he said: "Take it away," and it was placed before him the second night, and it occurred to him, and he said: "Take it away," and likewise the third night. So Thabit al-Bunani, Yazid al-Dabbi and Yahya al-Bakka' were told; they came and kept on at him until he drank a draught of sawiq (barley gruel). "On the Day (the earth) shakes": put in the accusative by what is in "with Us." "Al-rajfa": the earthquake and violent shaking. "Al-kathib": gathered sand, from "kathaba al-shay'" when he collected it, as if it were "fa'il" in the sense of "maf'ul" in origin. From it is "al-kathba" of milk. The ewe said: "Shear (me) a thick fleece and milk (me) a kathb quickly" [1] — meaning: they were like gathered sand that has been "hil" — "hilan," i.e., scattered and made to flow.
الحسن: أنه أمسى صائما، فأتى بطعام، فعرضت له هذه الآية، فقال: ارفعه، ووضع عنده الليلة الثانية، فعرضت له، فقال: ارفعه، وكذلك الليلة الثالثة، فأخبر ثابت البناني ويزيد الضبي ويحيى البكاء، فجاءوا فلم يزالوا به حتى شرب شربة من سويق يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ منصوب بما في لدينا. والرجفة: الزلزلة والزعزعة الشديدة. والكثيب: الرمل المجتمع من كثب الشيء إذا جمعه، كأنه فعيل بمعنى مفعول في أصله. ومنه الكثبة من اللبن، قالت الضائنة: أجز جفالا وأحلب كثبا «1» عجالا، أى: كانت مثل رمل مجتمع هيل هيلا، أى: نثر وأسيل.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 640
1. (1) . His statement "huwa alladhi": perhaps it should be "alladhi" without "huwa." ('A)
2. . Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih as a suspended report in (the book of) manners: "It is mentioned from Abu al-Darda'." And al-Bayhaqi connected it in "al-Shu'ab" in the sixth and fiftieth (chapter), by the route of Abu al-Ahwas, meaning the son of Ahwas ibn Hakim, from Abu al-Zahra', who said: Abu al-Darda' said. And Abu Nu'aym narrated it in "al-Hilya" in the biography of Abu al-Darda' by the route of Sufyan, from Khalaf ibn Hawshab, who said: Abu al-Darda' said, like al-Bayhaqi's narration.
3. . His statement "you need not get (al-zafar)": perhaps "in al-zafar." ('A)
4. . Narrated by Ahmad in "al-Zuhd" and al-Tabari by the route of Waki' from Hamza al-Zayyat from Humran ibn A'yan: "That the Prophet ﷺ (recited) this." And Ibn 'Adi narrated it from the narration of Abu Yusuf, from Hamza, from Hamdan, from Abu Harb ibn Abi al-Aswad. And others said that Yusuf narrates it from Hamza, from Hasab, from Humran.
1. (1) . قوله «هو الذي» لعله «الذي» بدون: هو. (ع)
2. . أخرجه البخاري في صحيحه تعليقا في الأدب: ويذكر عن أبى الدرداء. ووصله البيهقي في الشعب في السادس والخميسين من طريق أبى الأحوص يعنى ولد أحوص بن حكم عن أبى الزهراء قال قال أبو الدرداء. ورواه أبو نعيم في الحلية في ترجمة أبى الدرداء من طريق سفيان عن خلف بن حوشب قال قال أبو الدرداء مثل رواية البيهقي.
3. . قوله «لا تحتاج إلى الظفر» لعله: في الظفر. (ع)
4. . أخرجه أحمد في الزهد والطبري من طريق وكيع عن حمزة الزيات عن حمران بن أعين «أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بهذا» ورواه ابن عدى من رواية أبى يوسف عن حمزة عن حمدان عن أبى حرب بن أبى الأسود. وقال غيره: أن يوسف يرويه عن حمزة عن حسب عن حمران.
Vol. 4, p. 641
1. (1) . His statement "shear a thick fleece and milk a kathb": "al-jifal" is abundant wool. "Al-kathba" of milk is the measure of a milking; the plural is "kuthab" — so in al-Sihah. ('A)
2. . By Abu al-Tayyib. He says: worry diminishes the large-bodied man and cuts him down bit by bit. "Nahafa nahafatan": he became lean, leanly; so "nahafatan" is an absolute object, because it meets "ikhtirām" in meaning. It is possible that it is a specification, i.e., worry diminishes the great, big-bodied one in respect of the leanness that arises from it. It is also possible to make it an object of purpose, according to the view of one who does not require identity of the agent of the verb and the verbal noun. "Al-nasiya": the front of the head, i.e., the boy's head turns gray; and he specified the forelock because it is what faces the viewer when they meet, and the boy has hair only on his head; "wa-yahrim," i.e., the boy becomes old and weak.
1. (1) . قوله «وأجز جفالا وأحلب كثبا» الجفال: الصوف الكثير. والكثبة من اللبن: قدر حلبة، والجمع كثب، كذا في الصحاح. (ع)
2. . لأبى الطيب، يقول: ان الهم ينتقص الرجل الجسيم ويقتطعه شيئا فشيئا. ونحف نحافة: هزل هزالا، فنحافة مفعول مطلق، لأنها تلاقى الاحترام في المعنى. ويجوز أنها تمييز، أى: ينتقص الهم العظيم الجسيم من جهة النحافة الى تنشأ عنه. ويجوز جعلها مفعولا لأجله على مذهب من لم يشترط اتحاد الفعل والمصدر في الفاعل. والناصية: مقدم الرأس، أى: يشيب رأس الصبى. وخص الناصية، لأنها التي تقابل الناظر عند التقابل، ولا شعر الصبى إلا في رأسه، ويهرم، أى: يصير الصبى هرما ضعيفا.
08
Q 73:15–16 · Vol. 4, p. 641

Verses 15 to 16

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Indeed, We have sent to you a messenger as a witness over you, just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger (15) But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a severe seizure (16)
إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا إِلَيْكُمْ رَسُولاً شاهِداً عَلَيْكُمْ كَما أَرْسَلْنا إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولاً (15) فَعَصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ فَأَخَذْناهُ أَخْذاً وَبِيلاً (16)
Vol. 4, p. 641
The address is to the people of Mecca. "A witness over you": he will testify against you on the Day of Resurrection of your disbelief and denial.
الخطاب لأهل مكة شاهِداً عَلَيْكُمْ يشهد عليكم يوم القيامة بكفركم وتكذيبكم.
Question
If you ask: why was "messenger" indefinite and then definite?
فإن قلت: لم نكر الرسول ثم عرف؟
Answer
I say: because He meant: "We sent to Pharaoh one of the messengers"; and when He repeated it, being already mentioned, He introduced the definite lam as a pointer to the very one mentioned. "Wabil": heavy, thick, from their saying "kala' wabil," a pasture that is unwholesome and not digested because of its heaviness. "Al-wabil" is also the thick staff; from it is "al-wabil" for heavy rain.
قلت: لأنه أراد: أرسلنا إلى فرعون بعض الرسل، فلما أعاده وهو معهود بالذكر أدخل لام التعريف إشارة إلى المذكور بعينه وَبِيلًا ثقيلا غليظا، من قولهم: كلأ وبيل وخم لا يستمرأ لثقله. والوبيل: العصا الضخمة. ومنه الوابل للمطر العظيم.

Q 73:17–18 · Vol. 4, pp. 641–642

Verses 17 to 18

The verses as the commentary quotes them
So how can you protect yourselves, if you disbelieve, on a Day that will make children white-haired (17) The heaven will be split open by it; His promise is ever fulfilled (18)
فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْماً يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدانَ شِيباً (17) السَّماءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ كانَ وَعْدُهُ مَفْعُولاً (18)
Vol. 4, p. 641
"A Day" is an object, i.e., how can you guard yourselves on the Day of Resurrection, which belongs to it (the guarding), if you remain in disbelief and do not believe and do righteousness. It may also be an adverb of time, i.e., how will you have piety on the Day of Resurrection if you disbelieved in the world. It may also be put in the accusative by "kafartum," interpreted as "jahadtum" (you denied), i.e., how will you fear God and dread Him if you deny the Day of Resurrection and the recompense — because fear of God is dread of His punishment. "Makes children white-haired" is a proverb for severity; it is said of a severe day: "a day that turns children's forelocks white." The origin of it: that when worries and griefs accumulate upon a person, gray hair comes quickly upon him. Abu al-Tayyib said: "Worry wears down the big-bodied by thinness and turns the boy's forelock white and makes him old" [2]
يَوْماً مفعول به، أى: فكيف تقون أنفسكم يوم القيامة وهو له، إن بقيتم على الكفر. ولم تؤمنوا وتعملوا صالحا. ويجوز أن يكون ظرفا، أى: فكيف لكم بالتقوى في يوم القيامة إن كفرتم في الدنيا. ويجوز أن ينتصب بكفرتم على تأويل جحدتم، أى فكيف تتقون الله وتخشونه إن جحدتم يوم القيامة والجزاء: لأن تقوى الله خوف عقابه يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدانَ شِيباً مثل في الشدة يقال في اليوم الشديد: يوم يشيب نواصي الأطفال. والأصل فيه: أنّ الهموم والأحزان إذا تفاقمت على الإنسان. أسرع فيه الشيب. قال أبو الطيب: والهمّ يخترم الجسيم نحافة … ويشيب ناصية الصّبىّ ويهرم «2»
Vol. 4, p. 642
I have come across in some books that a man went to bed jet-black in hair like a raven's beak, and rose in the morning with head and beard white as the thaghama plant; he said: "I was shown the Resurrection, Paradise and the Fire in a dream, and I saw people being led in chains to the Fire; from the terror of that I have become as you see." It is also possible that the day is described as long, and that children reach in it the time of old age and white hair. "The heaven will be split open by it": a description of the day also by severity — and that the heaven, for all its greatness and firmness, is split open in it; so what do you suppose of other creatures? It has been read "munfatir" and "mutafattir." The meaning: "having splitting"; or by interpreting "heaven" as "roof"; or by interpreting it as "heaven is a thing that is split"; and the "ba'" in "bihi" is like that in your saying "I split the wood with the adze and it split by it," meaning: it splits by the severity of that day, which belongs to it, as a thing splits by what splits it. It is also possible that what is meant is: the heaven is burdened by it with a burden that leads to its splitting because of its greatness upon it and its dread of its occurrence, as in His words "It weighed heavily upon the heavens and the earth." "His promise" is an annexation of the verbal noun to its object, and the pronoun refers to the day. It is also possible that it is annexed to the subject, who is God, Mighty and Exalted, and no mention of Him preceded because He is known.
وقد مرّ بى في بعض الكتب أن رجلا أمسى فاحم الشعر كحنك الغراب، وأصبح وهو أبيض الرأس واللحية كالثغامة، فقال: أريت القيامة والجنة والنار في المنام، ورأيت الناس يقادون في السلاسل إلى النار، فمن هول ذلك أصبحت كما ترون. ويجوز أن يوصف اليوم بالطول. وأنّ الأطفال يبلغون فيه أوان الشيخوخة والشيب السَّماءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ وصف لليوم بالشدّة أيضا. وأنّ السماء على عظمها وإحكامها تنفطر فيه، فما ظنك بغيرها من الخلائق. وقرئ: منفطر ومتفطر. والمعنى: ذات انفطار. أو على تأويل السماء بالسقف. أو على تأويل السماء شيء منفطر، والباء في بِهِ مثلها في قولك: فطرت العود بالقدوم فانفطر به، يعنى: أنها تنفطر بشدة ذلك اليوم وهو له كما ينفطر الشيء بما يفطر به. ويجوز أن يراد السماء مثقلة به إثقالا يؤدّى إلى انفطارها لعظمه عليها وخشيتها من وقوعه، كقوله ثَقُلَتْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ. وَعْدُهُ من إضافة المصدر إلى المفعول، والضمير لليوم. ويجوز أن يكون مضافا إلى الفاعل وهو الله عز وعلا، ولم يجر له ذكر لسكونه معلوما.

10
Q 73:19 · Vol. 4, p. 642

Verse 19

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way (19)
إِنَّ هذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَنْ شاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلاً (19)
Vol. 4, p. 642
"Indeed, these": the verses that speak of severe threat "are a reminder": an admonition; so whoever wills, let him take heed by them and "take a way to his Lord" through piety and fear. The meaning of taking a way to Him is: drawing near and seeking access by obedience.
إِنَّ هذِهِ الآيات الناطقة بالوعيد الشديد تَذْكِرَةٌ موعظة فَمَنْ شاءَ اتعظ بها. واتخذ سبيلا إلى الله بالتقوى والخشية. ومعنى اتخاذ السبيل إليه: التقرّب والتوسل بالطاعة.
11
Q 73:20 · Vol. 4, pp. 642–644

Verse 20

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) a little less than two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, and a group of those with you; and God determines the night and the day. He knows that you will not be able to count it, so He has turned to you in forgiveness; so recite what is easy of the Qur'an. He knows that there will be among you those who are ill, and others traveling throughout the land seeking God's bounty, and others fighting in the cause of God. So recite what is easy of it, and establish prayer and give zakah and loan God a goodly loan. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with God — it is better and greater in reward. And seek forgiveness of God; indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful (20)
إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنى مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ وَطائِفَةٌ مِنَ الَّذِينَ مَعَكَ وَاللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ عَلِمَ أَنْ لَنْ تُحْصُوهُ فَتابَ عَلَيْكُمْ فَاقْرَؤُا ما تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ عَلِمَ أَنْ سَيَكُونُ مِنْكُمْ مَرْضى وَآخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَآخَرُونَ يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَاقْرَؤُا ما تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ وَأَقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً وَما تُقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْراً وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْراً وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (20)
Vol. 4, p. 643
"A little less than two-thirds of the night": less than the two; "adna," which is "nearer," was borrowed for "less," because when the distance between two things draws near, the spaces between them diminish, and when it is far, they increase. It has been read "wa-nisfahu wa-thuluthahu" with the accusative, meaning that you stand less than the two-thirds, and you stand the half and the third; and that corresponds to what came at the beginning of the Surah: the choice between standing the full half, standing less than it — which is the third — and standing more than it — which is "adna min thuluthayn." And it was read "wa-nisfihi wa-thuluthihi" with the genitive, i.e., you stand less than the two-thirds and less than the half and the third, and that corresponds to the choice between the half — which is less than the two-thirds; the third — which is less than the half; and the quarter — which is less than the third; and this is the last view. "And a group of those with you": a company of your companions stand for that. "And God determines the night and the day": no one is able to determine the night and the day and know the measures of their hours except God alone; and the fronting of His name, Mighty and Majestic, as the subject on which "yuqaddiru" is built is what indicates the sense of exclusivity in determining; the meaning is that you are not capable of it. The pronoun in "lan tuhsuhu" refers to the verbal noun of "yuqaddiru": that is, He knew that you cannot accurately keep the times, nor is their computation by adjustment and equalization achievable, unless you take the broader course for caution — and that is hard upon you, laborious for you. "So He has turned to you": an expression for permission to leave the determined standing, as in "so He turned to you and pardoned you; so now, lie with them." The meaning: He lifted the liability for leaving it from you, as liability is lifted from the one who repents. He expressed prayer by "recitation" because it is one of its pillars, just as He expressed it by "standing," "bowing" and "prostration." He means: "pray what is easy for you and not onerous of the night prayer"; and this abrogates the first, then both were abrogated by the five prayers. It is also said that it is the recitation of the Qur'an itself; it is said: let him recite a hundred verses; and whoever recites a hundred verses in a night, the Qur'an will not contend against him; and it is said: whoever recites a hundred verses is written among the devout; and it is said: fifty verses. And He explained the wisdom of the abrogation: it is the impossibility of standing for the sick, those traveling in the land for trade, and those fighting in the cause of God. It is also said: God made equal the fighters and those traveling to earn lawful income. From 'Abd God ibn Mas'ud ؓ: "Whichever man brings something to one of the Muslim cities, patient and seeking reward, and sells it at the day's price, he will be with God among the martyrs" [1]. From 'Abd God ibn 'Umar: "God has created no death I would die after being killed in God's cause more beloved to me than to die between the two saddle-pieces of a saddle, traveling in the land seeking God's bounty" [2]. And "He knew"
أَدْنى مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ أقل منهما، وإنما استعير الأدنى وهو الأقرب للأقل، لأن المسافة بين الشيئين إذا دنت: قل ما بينهما من الأحياز، وإذا بعدت كثر ذلك. وقرئ: ونصفه وثلثه بالنصب على أنك تقوم أقل من الثلثين، وتقوم النصف والثلث: وهو مطابق لما مرّ في أوّل السورة: من التخيير بين قيام النصف بتمامه وبين قيام الناقص منه- وهو الثلث- وبين قيام الزائد عليه- وهو الأدنى من الثلثين. وقرئ: ونصفه، وثلثه: بالجرّ، أى: تقوم أقل من الثلثين وأقل من النصف والثلث، وهو مطابق للتخيير بين النصف: وهو أدنى من الثلثين. والثلث: وهو أدنى من النصف. والربع: وهو أدنى من الثلث، وهو الوجه الأخير وَطائِفَةٌ مِنَ الَّذِينَ مَعَكَ ويقوم ذلك جماعة من أصحابك وَاللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ ولا يقدر على تقدير الليل والنهار ومعرفة مقادير ساعاتهما إلا الله وحده، وتقديم اسمه عز وجل مبتدأ مبنيا عليه يقدّر: هو الدال على معنى الاختصاص بالتقدير، والمعنى: أنكم لا تقدرون عليه، والضمير في لَنْ تُحْصُوهُ لمصدر يقدّر، أى علم أنه لا يصح منكم ضبط الأوقات ولا يتأتى حسابها بالتعديل والتسوية، إلا أن تأخذوا بالأوسع للاحتياط: وذلك شاق عليكم بالغ منكم فَتابَ عَلَيْكُمْ عبارة عن الترخيص في ترك القيام المقدّر، كقوله فَتابَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَعَفا عَنْكُمْ فَالْآنَ بَاشِرُوهُنَّ والمعنى: أنه رفع التبعة في تركه عنكم، كما يرفع التبعة عن التائب. وعبر عن الصلاة بالقراءة، لأنها بعض أركانها، كما عبر عنها بالقيام والركوع والسجود. يريد: فصلوا ما تيسر عليكم، ولم يتعذر من صلاة الليل، وهذا ناسخ للأوّل، ثم نسخا جميعا بالصلوات الخمس. وقيل هي قراءة القرآن بعينها، قيل: يقرأ مائة آية. ومن قرأ مائة آية في ليلة لم يحاجه القرآن، وقيل: من قرأ مائة آية كتب من القانتين. وقيل: خمسين آية. وقد بين الحكمة في النسخ. وهي تعذر القيام على المرضى، والضاربين في الأرض للتجارة، والمجاهدين في سبيل الله. وقيل: سوّى الله بين المجاهدين والمسافرين لكسب الحلال. وعن عبد الله بن مسعود رضى الله عنه: أيما رجل جلب شيأ إلى مدينة من مدائن المسلمين صابرا محتسبا، فباعه بسعر يومه: كان عند الله من الشهداء «1» . وعن عبد الله بن عمر: ما خلق الله موتة أموتها بعد القتل في سبيل الله أحب إلىّ من أن أموت بين شعبتى رحل: أضرب في الأرض أبتغى من فضل الله «2» . وعَلِمَ
Vol. 4, p. 644
a fresh statement in the form of an answer to a question about the reason for the abrogation. "And establish prayer": meaning the obligatory one; and "zakah": the obligatory one. It is also said: zakat al-fitr, because there was no zakah in Mecca; it was made obligatory only afterward; and whoever interprets it as the obligatory zakah makes the end of the Surah Medinan. "And loan God a goodly loan": He may mean all other charity, or the payment of zakah in the best manner — taking out the best of the wealth and what is most useful to the poor, observing the intention, seeking the face of God, and spending on those who deserve it — or every good thing done that relates to the self and wealth. "Khayran" is the second object of "wajada," and it is a separator (damir fasl). It is permissible even though it does not occur between two definites, because "af'al min" resembles a definite in its inability to take the definite article. Abu al-Sammal read "huwa khayrun wa-a'zamu ajran" with the nominative, as subject and predicate. From the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Whoever recites Surah al-Muzzammil, God will ward off hardship from him in this world and the Hereafter" [1].
استئناف على تقدير السؤال عن وجه النسخ وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ يعنى المفروضة والزكاة الواجبة وقيل: زكاة الفطر، لأنه لم يكن بمكة زكاة. وإنما وجبت بعد ذلك، ومن فسرها بالزكاة الواجبة جعل آخر السورة مدنيا وَأَقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً يجوز أن يريد: سائر الصدقات وأن يريد: أداء الزكاة على أحسن وجه: من إخراج أطيب المال وأعوده على الفقراء، ومراعاة النية وابتغاء وجه الله، والصرف إلى المستحق، وأن يريد: كل شيء يفعل من الخيز مما يتعلق بالنفس والمال خَيْراً ثانى مفعولي وجد. وهو فصل. وجاز وإن لم يقع بين معرفتين، لأنّ أفعل من أشبه في امتناعه من حرف التعريف المعرفة. وقرأ أبو السمال: هو خير وأعظم أجرا، بالرفع على الابتداء والخبر: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قرأ سورة المزمّل دفع الله عنه العسر في الدنيا والآخرة» «1» .
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 643
1. (1) . Narrated by al-Tha'labi from the narration of Farqad al-Sabakhi from Ibrahim from Ibn Mas'ud as his own statement; Farqad is weak. And Ibn Mardawayh connected it, mentioning 'Alqama ibn Ibrahim and 'Abd God, and also raised it to the Prophet, adding: then he recited "and others traveling throughout the land" — the verse.
2. . Narrated by al-Tha'labi from the narration of al-Qasim ibn 'Abd God from his father from Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar; its chain is weak. And Ibn Ma'bad narrated it in "al-Ta'a wa al-Ma'siya" from Ibn Wahb, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Nafi' that 'Umar said: "God has created no death I would die, except dying as a fighter in God's cause, more beloved to me than that I die — to the end." And al-Bayhaqi in "al-Shu'ab" in the thirteenth (chapter), by the route of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from 'Abd God: 'Umar or someone else mentioned, saying: "God has not created, to the end."
1. (1) . أخرجه الثعلبي من رواية فرقد السبخى عن إبراهيم عن ابن مسعود موقوفا. وفرقد ضعيف. ووصله ابن مردويه بذكر علقمة بن إبراهيم وعبد الله ورفعه أيضا. وزاد: ثم قرأ وَآخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ- الآية
2. . أخرجه الثعلبي من رواية القاسم بن عبد الله عن أبيه عن نافع عن ابن عمر به. وإسناده ضعيف. ورواه ابن معبد في الطاعة والمعصية عن ابن وهب عن يونس عن ابن شهاب عن نافع أن عمر قال «ما خلق الله موتة أموتها إلا أن أموت مجاهدا في سبيل الله أحب إلى من أن أموت- إلى آخره» والبيهقي في الشعب في الثالث عشر من طريق عبد الرزاق عن معمر عن الزهري عن عبد الله ذكر عمر أو غيره قال «ما خلق الله إلى آخره» .
Vol. 4, p. 644
1. (1) . Narrated by al-Tha'labi, al-Wahidi and Ibn Mardawayh with their chain to Ubayy ؓ.
2. . It has preceded in (Surah) Al 'Imran.
3. . Agreed upon from the narration of Abu Salama from him, and in a fuller form.
1. (1) . أخرجه الثعلبي والواحدي وابن مردويه بسندهم إلى أبى رضى الله عنه.
2. . تقدم في آل عمران.
3. . متفق عليه من رواية أبى سلمة عنه وأتم منه.
